Q: Check if current .NET version is still supported in C# A:

Sorry if I did not point this out clearly. It is a single application with multiple versions.

I already try to only support the latest few versions. But if there is any problem, I must fix it. I can only point out that the software is outdated, but the update planning is up to the customer.

The main problem is that if a customer wants to update, they need to update the complete software solution. Such updates can take up to a few weeks or even months as the solution is business critical. The main part of the solution is part of a closed system which is nearly zero security sensitive. This C# application is just a small optional extra software which runs almost exclusively on the intranet, but yes it is security sensitive.

Once a year I write down the changes of the latest versions. Then I check which customer uses outdated versions with critical problems. (e.g. outdated .NET 4.5, outdated SSL -  yes SSL) I forward this information and hope that one day the customer takes this information seriously.

But it even can be worse. A few years ago, I got a request to the predecessor software written in PHP.  Windows 2016 was outdated the customer requested if PHP software which requires PHP5 will run on windows 2019… I am not sure if there are still active versions of this software out there.

Q: Why does Float'Succ behave differently on Float-variables than on Float-expressions? A:

Float'Succ(Arg) is defined to "return the machine number immediately above the value of Arg" (ARM 2022 with 2025 additions, section 3.5). Consequently, Float'Succ(Pi) returns the machine number immediately above the value of Pi, Pi having a value of 3.14159_26535_89793....

I think it is a wrong interpretation. ARM 3.5 says this:

S'Succ denotes a function with the following specification: 

function S'Succ(Arg : S'Base)
  return S'Base

For an enumeration type, the function returns the value whose position number is one more than that of the value of Arg; Constraint_Error is raised if there is no such value of the type. For an integer type, the function returns the result of adding one to the value of Arg. For a fixed point type, the function returns the result of adding small to the value of Arg. For a floating point type, the function returns the machine number (as defined in 3.5.7) immediately above the value of Arg; Constraint_Error is raised if there is no such machine number.

S is Float. Arg is Float'Base. Float'Base is a single precision IEEE 754 floating-point number. It is not universal real. Thus Pi must be first converted to Float'Base by truncation or else by rounding and then the next single precision IEEE 754 number computed. If there is no such number Constraint_Error must propagate.

Q: How to verify/compare 2 values in Selenium? A:

Selenium Assertions are the best way you can use Assert to compare two values.

Assertions verify that the state of the application is same to what we are expecting. Selenium Assertions can be of three types: “assert”, “verify”, and ” waitFor”. When an “assert” fails, the test is aborted. When a “verify” fails, the test will continue execution, logging the failure. Available in 

import org.testng.Assert;

and perform 

Assert.assertEquals("one","two");

If you do not want your test to fail at a particular assertion and want to continue till the end and then assert, you can use SoftAsserts

You can read more about that here https://www.seleniumeasy.com/testng-tutorials/soft-asserts-in-testng-example
